newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro-court dismisses British gypsy's caravan case.
newsitem.headline: Euro-court dismisses British gypsy's caravan case.

text.p: The European Court of Human Rights dismissed on Wednesday a British gypsy's claim that the South Cambridgeshire District Council had violated her human rights by refusing to let her and her family live in three caravans on land she owned near the village of Willingham.

The council said Jane Buckley's caravans were an eyesore in a rural area, and suggested that she and her children live on an official site instead. But she refused, saying the official site was crime-ridden and not a fit place for a single mother with young children to live.

The European court ruled that Britain's planning permission and criminal justice laws did not violate gypsies' rights to follow their traditional lifestyle and that the reasons and means invoked in Buckley's case had not been excessive.

"It did not appear that the applicant had at any time been penalised or subjected to any detrimental treatment for attempting to follow a traditional gypsy lifestyle. In fact, it appeared that the relevant national policy had been aimed at enabling gypsies to cater for their own needs," the court said.
